pro_course_detail.description:
In this lesson we will conduct a practice IELTS speaking test, including all three parts. I will act as the examiner. After the mock test, I will give you feedback based on the public band descriptors, however I will not award you an official score.

I recommend having a good knowledge of the IELTS speaking test before doing mock tests.

pro_course_detail.title: IELTS Writing Mock Test (OFFLINE)
pro_course_detail.description:
This is an OFFLINE lesson. We will NOT meet in a call.

Do you want to practice an IELTS writing response and get helpful feedback? In this lesson, I will send you your choice of a Task 1 or Task 2 IELTS writing prompt that you must complete BEFORE the scheduled lesson time. I will give written corrections and feedback based on the IELTS public band descriptors on your writing document.

30 Minute lesson: One Task 1 /OR/ One Task 2 prompt
60 Minute lesson: Two Task 1 /OR/ Two Task 2 /OR/ One Task 1 & One Task 2

After booking, please message me which type of Task you would like, and whether you are taking the Academic or General Training IELTS test :)

Everyday Life: Discover the nuances of daily life in America, including common social practices, holidays, and traditions.

Language and Slang: Learn how Americans communicate, including popular slang, idiomatic expressions, and regional accents.

Cultural Etiquette: Understand the dos and don'ts of American culture to help you navigate social and professional situations with ease.

Pop Culture: Dive into American music, movies, TV shows, and literature to get a taste of what shapes contemporary American society.

History and Heritage: Explore significant historical events and figures that have influenced American culture and values.

Each lesson is interactive and tailored to your interests and goals, whether you're planning to visit, study, work, or simply want to deepen your cultural knowledge.

Join me for an engaging and informative journey into American culture. 

Let's make learning fun and enriching!

teacher_info.teaching_style: My general approach to language instruction is task-based. However, an understanding of grammar and vocabulary is important as well and are dealt with as needed in the context of communication. You will make phrases and I will give you feedback to help correct pronunciation and grammar. This part of the lesson is designed to give you a chance to learn and practice new vocabulary and phrases when you are outside and observing what is going on around you. You will start to think in English.

These will include PDFs, Videos, Quizzes and Discussion topics for you to use in your interactions with English speakers. The materials will be adjusted to your level and learning objectives.

3. The last part of the lesson will include a cultural component. This could be music and song lyrics, news videos or information about places to visit in an English speaking country.  This is a fun part of the lesson but also very important because language connects us as people, and making connections in business, work or socially is the goal of interacting with anyone.

With all lessons, you can choose if you want to focus more on a specific part or topic and I will design the lessons so you can make progress on your English journey and use what you learn in class.

teacher_info.intro:
After 25 years working in Information Technology (IT), I discovered that what I really wanted to do was to help people learn. For the last few years, I have been helping people like you become more confident speakers, regardless of the language they are learning - this, through one-on-one teaching and conversation practice here on italki.
I have been tutoring foreign languages part time since 1998. In 2016, I got involved full time, started teaching ESL locally, and mentored under the best teachers I could find. Learning and teaching Esperanto has broadened my knowledge of my own native English, and helped me learn how to explain things in a clear and understandable way.
teacher_info.introduction: In university, I completed a minor in German. Many of my friends were international students, often with limited English skills. I took pride in my ability to adapt my language to the appropriate level as they progressed. I learned Esperanto by email, but very soon my wife and I got involved with the community. We regularly sought opportunities to speak face to face. In a short time, the people I considered my mentors were seeking my input on how to express fine shades of meaning. Through two decades, I have seen a broad range of backgrounds. Different explanations work for different people. Some aspects need more attention. Some common explanations are actually best avoided. Since Esperanto was our home language, I have accumulated songs, games, and other methods that are suitable for younger children. M y 11 year old son and I created a course. I volunteer with the boy scouts, teaching and mentoring boys from 6-17. Through organizing Esperanto events, I have the opportunity to work with both beginners and more experienced self-learners who find themselves speaking Esperanto for the first time. This can be scary, but we've all been there. I can help you over these jitters, and to move beyond translating phrases to actively thinking in the language. This is an exciting time for Esperanto. New technology allows us not only to read and write, but for conversation as well. You need a teacher with experience actually speaking the language. It's good to start with good pronunciation, but it's never too late. NOTE FOR ENGLISH LEARNERS: Although my profile emphasizes other languages, I want you to know that I take teaching English seriously. I teach English locally and work with students from total beginner to near-native - ages 8 to 80. I will encourage you to work on your communication skills and being understood. I will also provide feedback on one or two things you can work on. I invite you to read the comments by others who have learned English with me.

Now I am well-known in the Esperanto community - a regular teacher-in-residence at NASK and other events. In 1988 I became a tutor in a Free Esperanto Course (which I now administer), and when I left my IT career in 2016, I started teaching once a week at the local ESOL Association, as well as tutoring on line and in person. Teaching different languages in these situations has given me a unique perspective.
teacher_info.teaching_style:
The main thing is that I want my students to speak. The first step is to feel comfortable. You will receive solid feedback, but you don't need to worry about being constantly corrected or about making mistakes. You're going to make mistakes. We can expect that ahead of time. The important thing is that we learn in the process.
For English, once you're ready to try your first conversation, I will help you get to the next level -  including intermediate and advanced English, accent reduction, and Business English. For German, I like to help people get started right in the beginning, or to help if you're struggling with understanding German grammar. For Esperanto, I cover the whole range.
